'''Jorge Iván Gutiérrez Cárdenas''' (born December 27, 1988) is a Mexican former professional [[basketball]] player currently working as an assistant coach for the [[Long Island Nets]] of the [[NBA G League]]. He played [[college basketball]] for the [[California Golden Bears men's basketball|California Golden Bears]]. He is considered one the best Mexican basketball players of all time.

==High school career==
Gutiérrez attended [[Abraham Lincoln High School (Denver)|Abraham Lincoln High School]] for two years, leading the Lancers to the Colorado state championship, earning tournament MVP honors after contributing 22.5 points and 6.0 rebounds on 58.8 percent field goal shooting over the course of the campaign. The next year, he averaged 20.3 points and 3.7 rebounds while shooting 61.4 percent from the floor. After two years, he moved to [[The Henderson International School|Findlay Prep]] where he averaged 13.4 points, 6.0 rebounds, 2.7 steals and 2.6 assists as a senior, earning the MVP award at the National Prep School Invitational in Rhode Island after helping his team to a runner-up finish.<ref name="bio">{{cite web|url=http://www.calbears.com/news/2013/4/17/208187449.aspx|title=Jorge Gutierrez Bio|work=CalBears.com|access-date=September 26, 2016}}</ref>

==College career==
Gutiérrez was recruited by coach [[Mike Montgomery (basketball)|Mike Montgomery]] to play at the [[University of California, Berkeley]]. In his senior year with the [[California Golden Bears men's basketball|Golden Bears]] in 2011–12, Gutiérrez was named the 2012 [[Pac-12 Conference Men's Basketball Player of the Year|Pac-12 Conference Player of the Year]], as well as the conference's [[Pac-12 Conference Men's Basketball Defensive Player of the Year|Defensive Player of the Year]]<ref>{{cite news|last=Brennan |first=Eammonn |title=Is Pac-12 primed for wild finish? |date=February 8, 2012 |work=ESPN.com |url=https://www.espn.com/mens-college-basketball/champweek2012/story/_/id/7655799/pac-12-tournament-primer-college-basketball |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20120309234528/http://espn.go.com/mens-college-basketball/champweek2012/story/_/id/7655799/pac-12-tournament-primer-college-basketball |archive-date=March 9, 2012 |url-status=live }}</ref><ref>{{cite news|last=Faraudo |first=Jeff |title=Cal's Jorge Gutierrez named Pac-12 Player of the Year |date=March 5, 2012 |work=MercuryNews.com |url=http://www.mercurynews.com/breaking-news/ci_20106639/cals-jorge-gutierrez-named-pac-12-player-year |archive-url=https://archive.today/20130128191051/http://www.mercurynews.com/breaking-news/ci_20106639/cals-jorge-gutierrez-named-pac-12-player-year |archive-date=January 28, 2013 |url-status=dead }}</ref> after averaging 13 points, 5.3 rebounds, 4.1 assists and 1.2 steals. He also earned [[List of All-Pac-12 Conference men's basketball teams|All-Pac-12]] honors in 2011 and 2012.<ref>{{cite web |publisher=SB Nation |work=BuildingTheDam.com |url=http://www.buildingthedam.com/2012/3/5/2847531/jorge-gutierrez-pac-12-player-of-the-year-jared-cunningham-named-to |title=Jorge Gutierrez Pac-12 Player of the Year, Jared Cunningham Named to First Team |date=March 5, 2012 |access-date=March 22, 2012}}</ref>

==Professional career==
===Pioneros de Quintana Roo (2012)===
After going undrafted in the [[2012 NBA draft]], Gutiérrez joined the [[Denver Nuggets]] for the 2012 NBA Summer League.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.nba.com/summer-league/2012/teams/nuggets/ |title=2012 Nuggets Summer League Team |work=NBA.com |access-date=July 10, 2012}}</ref> In August 2012, he tried out for [[KK Partizan|Partizan]] of [[Basketball League of Serbia|Serbia]]<ref>{{cite news|title=Partizan brings in Jorge Gutierrez and Matias Bartolin for try-out |work=LatinBasket.com |date=August 13, 2012 |url=https://www.latinbasket.com/Mexico/basketball.aspx?NewsID=283517 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20140320191555/http://www.latinbasket.com/Mexico/basketball.asp?NewsID=283517 |archive-date=March 20, 2014 |url-status=live }}</ref> but was subsequently not signed. On October 3, 2012, he joined [[Pioneros de Quintana Roo]] of Mexico for the rest of the 2012 LNBP season.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.seleccionmexicanadebaloncesto.com/2012/10/jorge-gutierrez-se-integra-pioneros-de.html|title=Jorge Gutiérrez se integra a Pioneros de Quintana Roo|work=SeleccionMexicanaDeBaloncesto.com|date=October 3, 2012|language=es|access-date=November 6, 2013}}</ref> He played his tenth and final game for Pioneros on November 3, 2012, recording 9 points, 4 assists, 2 rebounds, 2 steals and 1 block.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.eurobasket.com/boxScores/Mexico/2012/1103_17445_9740.asp?|title=Regular Season Round 20: Gigantes - Pioneros 73-103|work=Eurobaket.com|date=November 3, 2012|access-date=November 3, 2012}}</ref>

===Canton Charge (2012–2014)===
On November 2, 2012, he was selected by the [[Cleveland Charge|Canton Charge]] in the second round of the 2012 NBA D-League draft.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.nba.com/dleague/canton/news/charge_announce_201213_traini_2012_11_06.html|title=Charge Announce 2012-13 Training Camp Roster|work=NBA.com|date=November 6, 2012|access-date=November 16, 2013|url-status=dead|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20131209031855/http://www.nba.com/dleague/canton/news/charge_announce_201213_traini_2012_11_06.html|archive-date=December 9, 2013}}</ref>

In July 2013, Gutiérrez joined the Sacramento Kings for the [[2013 NBA Summer League]]. On September 30, 2013, he signed with the [[Brooklyn Nets]].<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.nba.com/nets/news/brooklyn-nets-announce-training-camp-roster|title=Brooklyn Nets Announce Training Camp Roster|work=NBA.com|date=September 30, 2013|access-date=September 30, 2013}}</ref> However, he was later waived by the Nets on October 26, 2013.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.insidehoops.com/blog/?p=14651|title=Brooklyn Nets waive Jorge Gutierrez, Chris Johnson and Adonis Thomas|work=InsideHoops.com|date=October 26, 2013|access-date=October 26, 2013}}</ref> In November 2013, he was re-acquired by the Canton Charge.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.nba.com/dleague/canton/news/canton_charge_announce_201314_2013_11_06.html |title=Canton Charge 2013-14 Training Camp Roster |work=NBA.com |date=November 6, 2013 |access-date=November 6, 2013 |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20140203081253/http://www.nba.com/dleague/canton/news/canton_charge_announce_201314_2013_11_06.html |archive-date=February 3, 2014 }}</ref>

===Brooklyn Nets (2014)===
On March 6, 2014, he signed a 10-day contract with the Brooklyn Nets.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.nba.com/nets/news/nets-sign-jorge-gutierrez-10-day-contract|title=Nets Sign Jorge Gutierrez to 10-Day Contract|work=NBA.com|date=March 6, 2014|access-date=March 6, 2014}}</ref> On March 9, 2014, he made his NBA debut in a 104–89 win over the [[Sacramento Kings]], making him the fourth Mexican to play in the NBA after [[Horacio Llamas]], [[Eduardo Nájera]], and [[Gustavo Ayón]]. In just under 5 minutes of playing time, he recorded 1 point and 1 steal.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.nba.com/games/20140309/SACBKN/gameinfo.html|title=Notebook: Nets 104, Kings 89|work=NBA.com|date=March 9, 2014|access-date=March 9, 2014}}</ref> On March 17, 2014, he signed a second 10-day contract with the Nets.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.nba.com/nets/news/nets-sign-jorge-gutierrez-second-10-day-contract |title=Nets Sign Jorge Gutierrez to a Second 10-Day Contract |work=NBA.com |date=March 17, 2014 |access-date=March 17, 2014 |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20140322031453/http://www.nba.com/nets/news/nets-sign-jorge-gutierrez-second-10-day-contract |archive-date=March 22, 2014 }}</ref> On March 21, 2014, he recorded an NBA career high 10 points, along with 3 rebounds, 1 assist and 1 block, in 114–98 victory over the Boston Celtics.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.nba.com/games/20140321/BOSBKN/gameinfo.html|title=Notebook: Nets 114, Celtics 98|work=NBA.com|date=March 21, 2014|access-date=March 21, 2014}}</ref> On March 28, 2014, he signed a multi-year deal with the Nets.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.nba.com/nets/news/nets-sign-jorge-gutierrez-multi-year-contract|title=Nets Sign Jorge Gutierrez to Multi-Year Contract|work=NBA.com|date=March 28, 2014|access-date=March 28, 2014}}</ref>

In July 2014, Gutiérrez joined the Brooklyn Nets for the [[2014 NBA Summer League]].<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.nba.com/nets/news/brooklyn-nets-announce-summer-league-roster|title=Brooklyn Nets Announce Summer League Roster|work=NBA.com|date=July 1, 2014|access-date=July 1, 2014}}</ref>

On December 11, 2014, Gutiérrez was traded, along with [[Andrei Kirilenko]], the Nets' second round draft pick in 2020 and the right to swap second round picks in 2018, to the [[Philadelphia 76ers]] in exchange for [[Brandon Davies]].<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.nba.com/sixers/news/141211-trade|title=Sixers Complete Trade With Nets|work=NBA.com|date=December 11, 2014|access-date=December 11, 2014}}</ref> The next day, he was waived by the 76ers.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.nba.com/sixers/news/141212-roberts-call-up|title=Sixers Call Up Ronald Roberts From Delaware 87ers|work=NBA.com|date=December 12, 2014|access-date=December 12, 2014}}</ref>

===Canton Charge / Milwaukee Bucks (2014–2016)===
[[File:Jorge_Gutiérrez_(basketball).jpg|thumb|right|250px|Jorge Gutiérrez playing with the [[California Golden Bears]].]]
On December 23, 2014, Gutiérrez was reacquired by the Canton Charge.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.cantonrep.com/article/20141223/SPORTS/141229722|title=Jorge Gutierrez is returning to the Charge|work=CantonRep.com|date=December 23, 2014|access-date=December 23, 2014}}</ref> On January 28, 2015, Gutiérrez signed a 10-day contract with the [[Milwaukee Bucks]], reuniting with his former Brooklyn Nets coach, [[Jason Kidd]].<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.nba.com/bucks/release/bucks-sign-gutierrez-10-day-contract|title=BUCKS SIGN GUTIERREZ TO A 10-DAY CONTRACT|work=NBA.com|date=January 28, 2015|access-date=January 28, 2015}}</ref> On February 7, he signed a second 10-day contract with the Bucks.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.nba.com/bucks/bucks-sign-gutierrez-second-10-day-contract|title=BUCKS SIGN GUTIERREZ TO SECOND 10-DAY CONTRACT|work=NBA.com|date=February 7, 2015|access-date=February 7, 2015}}</ref> He parted ways with the Bucks on February 17 after the team did not sign him for the rest of the season. On March 4, he was reacquired by Canton.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.oursportscentral.com/services/releases/?id=4933759|title=Charge Reacquire Jorge Gutierrez|work=OurSportsCentral.com|date=March 4, 2015|access-date=March 4, 2015}}</ref> On April 7, he returned to the Bucks, signing a multi-year deal with the team.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.nba.com/bucks/release/bucks-sign-jorge-gutierrez|title=BUCKS SIGN JORGE GUTIERREZ|work=NBA.com|date=April 7, 2015|access-date=April 7, 2015}}</ref> On October 21, 2015, he was waived by the Bucks.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.nba.com/bucks/release/bucks-request-waivers-three-players|title=BUCKS REQUEST WAIVERS ON THREE PLAYERS|work=NBA.com|date=October 21, 2015|access-date=October 21, 2015}}</ref>

On December 10, 2015, Gutiérrez was reacquired by the Canton Charge.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://canton.dleague.nba.com/news/jorge-gutierrez-returns-to-charge/|title=Gutierrez Returns to Charge|work=NBA.com|date=December 10, 2015|access-date=December 10, 2015|archive-date=December 22, 2015|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20151222074506/http://canton.dleague.nba.com/news/jorge-gutierrez-returns-to-charge/|url-status=dead}}</ref> The next day, he made his 2015–16 debut in a 110–107 win over the [[Iowa Energy]], recording nine points, four rebounds, five assists and four steals in 29 minutes.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://dleague.nba.com/games/20151211/IWACTN/|title=Dunigan, Harris Help Charge Earn OT Win|work=NBA.com|date=December 11, 2015|access-date=February 20, 2016|archive-date=March 4, 2016|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160304192732/http://dleague.nba.com/games/20151211/IWACTN/|url-status=dead}}</ref>

===Charlotte Hornets (2016)===
On February 20, 2016, Gutiérrez signed a 10-day contract with the [[Charlotte Hornets]].<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.nba.com/hornets/hornets-sign-gutierrez-10-day-contract|title=Hornets Sign Gutierrez to 10-Day Contract|work=NBA.com|date=February 20, 2016|access-date=February 20, 2016}}</ref> Four days later, he made his debut for the Hornets in a 114–103 loss to the [[Cleveland Cavaliers]], recording four points, two assists and one steal in four minutes off the bench.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.nba.com/games/20160224/CHACLE/gameinfo.html|title=James, Irving lead Cavaliers past Hornets, 114-103|work=NBA.com|date=February 24, 2016|access-date=February 28, 2016|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170801005938/http://www.nba.com/games/20160224/CHACLE/gameinfo.html|archive-date=August 1, 2017|url-status=dead}}</ref> He went on to sign a second 10-day contract with the Hornets on March 1,<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.nba.com/hornets/hornets-sign-jorge-gutierrez-second-10-day-contact|title=Hornets Sign Jorge Gutierrez to Second 10-Day Contact|work=NBA.com|date=March 1, 2016|access-date=March 1, 2016}}</ref> and then a rest-of-season contract on March 11.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.nba.com/hornets/press-releases/hornets-sign-jorge-gutierrez-remainder-2015-16-season|title=Hornets Sign Jorge Gutierrez for Remainder of 2015-16 Season|work=NBA.com|date=March 11, 2016|access-date=March 11, 2016}}</ref>

On September 26, 2016, Gutiérrez signed with the [[Brooklyn Nets]], returning to the franchise for a second stint.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.nba.com/nets/news/2016/09/26/brooklyn-nets-sign-chase-budinger-and-jorge-gutierrez|title=Brooklyn Nets Sign Chase Budinger and Jorge Gutierrez|work=NBA.com|date=September 26, 2016|access-date=September 26, 2016}}</ref> However, he was later waived by the Nets on October 18 after appearing in three preseason games.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.nba.com/nets/news/2016/10/18/brooklyn-nets-waive-beech-budinger-gutierrez-and-mockevicius|title=Brooklyn Nets Waive Beech, Budinger, Gutierrez and Mockevicius|work=NBA.com|date=October 18, 2016|access-date=October 18, 2016}}</ref>

===Trabzonspor (2016–2017)===
On November 8, 2016, Gutiérrez signed a deal with Turkish club [[Trabzonspor B.K.|Trabzonspor]].<ref>{{cite news|title=Trabzonspor lands Jorge Gutierrez|url=http://www.sportando.com/en/europe/turkey/216800/trabzonspor-lands-jorge-gutierrez.html|access-date=November 8, 2016|work=Sportando.com|date=November 8, 2016}}</ref>

On June 30, 2017, Gutierrez signed on to play for the Portland Trail Blazers NBA Summer League team.<ref>{{Cite web|url=http://www.nba.com/blazers/trail-blazers-announce-2017-summer-league-roster|title=Trail Blazers Announce 2017 Summer League Roster|website=[[NBA.com]] }}</ref>

===Delteco GBC (2018–2019)===
On August 28, 2018, Gutiérrez signed a one-year deal with [[San Sebastián Gipuzkoa BC|Delteco GBC]] of the [[Liga ACB]].<ref>{{cite news |title=ACB.COM - Jorge Gutiérrez, experiencia NBA para dirigir a Delteco GBC |url=http://www.acb.com/redaccion.php?id=142880 |access-date=28 August 2018 |work=www.acb.com |date=28 August 2018 |language=es-ES |archive-date=August 29, 2018 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180829072123/http://www.acb.com/redaccion.php?id=142880 |url-status=dead }}</ref>

On January 29, 2019, the Basque club parted ways with Gutiérrez.<ref>{{cite news |title=Gipuzkoa, Jorge Gutierrez part ways |url=https://sportando.basketball/en/gipuzkoa-jorge-gutierrez-part-ways/ |access-date=17 February 2019 |work=Sportando |date=29 January 2019 }}</ref>

===Hamburg Towers (2019–2020)===
On November 4, 2019, [[Hamburg Towers]] announced that they had signed Gutiérrez.<ref>{{cite web|title=EX-NBA-AKTEUR JORGE GUTIERREZ VERSTÄRKT TOWERS|language=DE|url=https://www.hamburgtowers.de/ex-nba-akteur-jorge-gutierrez-verstaerkt-towers|date=November 4, 2019|website=hamburgtowers.de|access-date=November 4, 2019}}</ref> He averaged 14.2 points, 3.8 rebounds and 5.9 assists per game with Hamburg.<ref name=gottingen>{{Cite web|url=https://www.eurobasket.com/Germany/news/638924/Goettingen-signs-Jorge-Gutierrez|title=Goettingen signs Jorge Gutierrez|date=August 1, 2020|publisher=Eurobasket|language=En|access-date=August 1, 2020}}</ref>

===Göttingen (2020–2021)===
On August 1, 2020, Gutiérrez signed with [[BG Göttingen]] of the [[Basketball Bundesliga]].<ref>{{Cite news|url=https://sportando.basketball/en/jorge-gutierrez-officially-joins-bg-gottingen/|title=Jorge Gutierrez officially joins BG Gottingen|date=August 1, 2020|newspaper=Sportando|language=En|access-date=January 16, 2021}}</ref>

===Peristeri (2021)===
On January 15, 2021, Gutiérrez signed with [[Peristeri B.C.|Peristeri]] of the [[Greek Basket League]].<ref>{{Cite news|url=https://sportando.basketball/en/peristeri-signs-jorge-gutierrez/|title=Peristeri signs Jorge Gutierrez
|date=January 15, 2021|newspaper=Sportando|language=En|access-date=January 16, 2021}}</ref> Gutiérrez averaged 8.4 points, 2.4 rebounds, 2.4 assists, and 1.1 steals per game.<ref name="astros" />

===Astros de Jalisco (2021–2022)===
On September 2, 2021, Gutiérrez signed with [[Astros de Jalisco]] of the [[Liga Nacional de Baloncesto Profesional]] (LNBP).<ref name="astros">{{cite web |title=Astros ink Jorge Gutierrez |url=https://www.latinbasket.com/Mexico/news/703029/Astros-ink-Jorge-Gutierrez |website=Latinbasket |access-date=September 2, 2021 |date=September 2, 2021}}</ref> He was named the Mexican MVP of the [[2022 LNBP season|2022 season]].<ref>{{cite news|url=https://www.milenio.com/deportes/basquetbol/jorge-gutierrez-mvp-lnbp-valdeolmillos-coach|title=Reconocen a Jorge Gutiérrez como el MVP de la temporada en la LNBP; Valdeolmillos mejor coach|work=[[Milenio]]|first=Carlos|last=Meza|date=23 September 2022|access-date=18 December 2022|language=es}}</ref>

===Dorados Capital (2022)===
On January 28, 2022, Gutiérrez signed with Dorados Capital of the Liga de Básquetbol Estatal de Chihuahua (LBE),<ref>{{cite web|title=Se incorpora el exjugador de la NBA Jorge Gutiérrez a Dorados Capital|url=https://elpuntero.com.mx/inicio/2022/01/28/se-incorpora-el-exjugador-de-la-nba-jorge-gutierrez-a-dorados-capital/|website=ElPuntero.com.mx|date=January 28, 2022|access-date=August 21, 2024|language=Spanish}}</ref> helping the team win a title, while being named Finals MVP.<ref>{{cite web|first=Sergio|last=Juárez|title=Dorados logra la sexta corona en la Liga Estatal de Basquetbol|url=https://www.elheraldodechihuahua.com.mx/deportes/dorados-logra-la-sexta-corona-en-la-liga-estatal-de-basquetbol-8098435.html|website=ElHeraldoDeChihuahua.com.mx|date=April 6, 2022|access-date=August 21, 2024|language=Spanish}}</ref>

===Libertadores de Querétaro (2022–2023)===
On November 27, 2022, Gutiérrez signed with [[Libertadores de Querétaro]] of the [[Liga Nacional de Baloncesto Profesional]].<ref>{{cite web|first=Marcos|last=Arellano|title=Jorge Gutiérrez llega como fichaje "bomba" de Libertadores de Querétaro|url=https://www.diariodequeretaro.com.mx/deportes/jorge-gutierrez-llega-como-fichaje-bomba-de-libertadores-de-queretaro-9249172.html|website=DiarioDeQueretaro.com.mx|date=November 27, 2022|access-date=August 21, 2024|language=Spanish}}</ref>

===Apaches de Chihuahua (2024)===
On January 15, 2024, Gutiérrez signed with Apaches de Chihuahua of the Liga de Básquetbol Estatal de Chihuahua.<ref>{{cite web|first=Sergio|last=Juárez|title=¡Listo para la LBE 2024! Jorge Gutiérrez es el nuevo integrante de Apaches de Chihuahua|url=https://www.elheraldodechihuahua.com.mx/deportes/listo-para-la-lbe-2024-jorge-gutierrez-es-el-nuevo-integrante-de-apaches-de-chihuahua-11290967.html|website=ElHeraldoDeChihuahua.com.mx|date=January 15, 2024|access-date=August 21, 2024|language=Spanish}}</ref> On August 20, he announced his retirement from professional basketball.<ref>{{cite web|first=Sebastián|last=Gómez|title=Jorge Gutiérrez anuncia su retiro del Básquetbol|url=https://mexico.as.com/masdeporte/jorge-gutierrez-anuncia-su-retiro-del-basquetbol-n/|website=AS.com|date=August 20, 2024|access-date=August 21, 2024|language=Spanish}}</ref>

==National team career==
In 2013, Gutiérrez made his debut for the [[Mexico national basketball team|Mexican national basketball team]] at the [[2013 FIBA Americas Championship]]. He went on represent Mexico at the [[2014 FIBA Basketball World Cup]] where he averaged 9.2 points per game.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://archive.fiba.com/pages/eng/fa/player/p/pid/109772/sid/6584/tid/328/_/2013_FIBA_Americas_Championship_for_Men/index.html|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20130916153025/http://archive.fiba.com/pages/eng/fa/player/p/pid/109772/sid/6584/tid/328/_/2013_FIBA_Americas_Championship_for_Men/index.html|url-status=dead|archive-date=September 16, 2013|title=Jorge Gutierrez's profile – FIBA.com|work=FIBA.com|access-date=October 21, 2015}}</ref>

==Coaching career==
On September 12, 2024, Gutiérrez was hired by the [[Long Island Nets]] of the [[NBA G League]] to be an assistant coach.<ref>{{cite web|title=Long Island Nets Announce Coaching Staff|url=https://www.oursportscentral.com/services/releases/long-island-nets-announce-coaching-staff/n-6147082|website=OurSportsCentral.com|date=September 12, 2024|access-date=September 13, 2024}}</ref>

==Personal life==
The son of Fernando Gutiérrez and Bertha Cárdenas, he has two brothers, Fernando and Julián. He includes drawing among his hobbies and majored in interdisciplinary studies.<ref name="bio" />
